key_insight: An event-driven Monte Carlo repair-logistics model can exploit mandatory hold periods to opportunistically insert inverter repairs and boost throughput without adding facility capacity.
engineering_relevance: For utility-scale PV fleets, better repair scheduling directly improves inverter availability, grid reliability, and lifecycle economics.
method: Models the full centralized repair cycle: admin wait, transport, repair, and return-to-inventory.
Uses parallel production lines with opportunistic insertion during idle hold periods.
Calibrates stage durations with a two-component heavy-tail mixture and health-driven repair completion.
evidence_signal: The model was calibrated on 43 field-observed repairs and matched the empirical bimodal repair-duration distribution with a one-dimensional Wasserstein distance of 53.3 days.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate hold-period and delay-distribution assumptions, so performance may vary when repair policies or fleet behavior differ from the observed data.
paper_title: Probabilistic Repair Logistics Modeling for Utility-Scale PV Inverter Fleets Using Event-Driven Simulation
